memo:
HOURS AND PROOF CONFIRMED; PRACTICAL BARRIERS REQUIRE IMMEDIATE NAVIGATOR HELP.

Clock: 5.6 days remain (due 2026-07-23 23:59). Deadline has not passed.

Screening results:
— Hours: 84/month employment meets the 80-hour standard (DOC-WORK: "Pay stubs covering the month are the cleanest proof of employment hours").
— Evidence: Pay stubs on hand for the claimed activity; no documents missing.
— Exemptions: None claimed or found.

HOWEVER, screening flags two critical barriers:
1. Mail from agency returned before at this address — notice address may be stale (RT-NOTICE: "If mail has been returned, the state must attempt other contact methods").
2. No reliable internet access — online portal cannot be the only reporting plan.

These are the conditions under which eligible people lose coverage procedurally. The member is compliant and has the proof, but with 5 days left, no internet, and mail delivery risk, a certified navigator or legal-aid office must help immediately to:
— Confirm the current address on file and, if needed, update it.
— Select the safest submission channel: phone (REQ-DEMOSTATE: "Demo State accepts reporting... by phone through the state help line") or in-person at county office (safest given mail risk).
— Keep a confirmation number (DL-RESPOND: "keep a copy or a confirmation number for anything you submit").
— If the address cannot be verified or mail is refused again, the 90-day reconsideration window exists (DL-RECON: "If coverage is terminated for a procedural reason — missing paperwork, an unanswered notice — there is a 90-day reconsideration period after the termination date"), but preventing termination now is far safer.

Refer to certified navigator, community health worker, legal aid, or state Medicaid ombudsman without delay (RT-HELP).
member_impact:
Good news: you are doing the work. You have 84 hours a month, and you have your pay stubs to prove it. That meets what the state is asking for.

But we need to be careful about HOW you send them in. Your mail has had problems in the past, and you do not have internet at home. With only five days left, we need to get you help right now so the papers get where they need to go and nothing gets lost.

Please call a Medicaid navigator or your legal-aid office TODAY. You can find them by calling the state help line (the number is on your notice). Tell them: "My mail has been returned before, I do not have internet, and I have five days to send in my work hours proof."

They will help you pick the safest way to send your pay stubs — maybe by phone, maybe in person at the county office. They will also make sure the state has the right address for you.

You have the proof you need. We just need to make sure it gets there safely. Do not delay — call today.
recommended_actions: Contact a certified Medicaid navigator, community health worker, legal-aid office, or state Medicaid ombudsman TODAY to secure immediate help with submission channel and address verification.
Confirm current mailing address on file with the state before submitting (may have changed since prior returned mail).
Plan submission through non-mail channel: phone (state help line) or in-person at county office — do NOT rely on mail given history of returns.
Keep confirmation number or written proof of submission, whatever channel is used (per DL-RESPOND).
Have pay stubs ready and with the helper when they assist.

citations.quote: Pay stubs covering the month are the cleanest proof of employment hours.
Demo State (synthetic) accepts reporting online through the member portal, by phone through the state help line, by mail using the form attached to the notice, and in person at a county office.
If mail has been returned, the state must attempt other contact methods.

Responding through any accepted channel by that date — with even a partial packet plus a note about what is coming — is far better than silence. Silence is what turns a paperwork question into a termination.
If coverage is terminated for a procedural reason — missing paperwork, an unanswered notice — there is a 90-day reconsideration period after the termination date.
Certified navigators, community health workers, legal-aid offices, and the state Medicaid ombudsman help with renewals, exemptions, and hearings at no charge.

findings.detail: Only 6 days remain to respond (due 2026-07-23T23:59:00). If more time is genuinely needed, the 30-day cure window after a non-compliance notice is a safety net — but do not plan on it.
Qualifying hours: 84 per month (84h employment) — meets the 80-hour standard.
Every claimed activity (1) has an accepted document on hand.

Practical barriers present: mail from the agency has been returned before — the notice address may be stale; verify it and ask for electronic notices | no reliable internet access — the online portal cannot be the only reporting plan; identify the phone and paper channels now. These are the conditions under which eligible people lose coverage procedurally — involve a navigator or legal-aid office.
